headline: Stage 3d answer: training at the hard setting makes a worse partner
lede: The RL lab's #2621 closed with a clean negative — an imitation model trained on the hard stamp (slack + wizard hero) wins ZERO of 24 fresh held-out games where the default-trained v4 wins four, and it repeats the failure on validation. The hard corpus teaches the partner to survive by staying away, and a goal-trained bodyguard model games its own goal from that starting point by ending the game early. Six failure modes now on the shelf.

notes.text: Export stamp flags (retrogames #2633) merged — hard-setting corpora are exportable through the front door now, replay-verifiable and byte-deterministic.
Held-out 906..929 scored once each: cpu 24/24, v4 4/24, v5 0/24, bodyguard-v2h 0/24 (avgLv 0), progress-v2h 2/24. Goal objectives moved; partnership did not.
Goal economics are warm-start-dependent: 3c's honest winner (bodyguard) collapses to hide-and-exit when retrained from the disengaged warm start — the starting point matters as much as the goal.
Matrix self-tests were quietly red on three stale pins (a 1e-9 tolerance died at the first 24-game range); refreshed to 13/13 with a discovery pin for the new held-out range.
